entities.name: Æthelfrith of Northumbria
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Æthelfrith was King of Bernicia from c. 593 until his death around 616 AD at the Battle of the River Idle. He became the first Bernician king to also rule the neighbouring land of Deira, giving him an important place in the development and the unification of the later kingdom of Northumbria. Reigning from the late 6th century until his death, he was known for his military campaigns against the Britons and his victory over the Gaels of Dál Riata. His most famous victory came at the Battle of Chester, where he decisively defeated a coalition of British forces, significantly weakening the influence of the native Britons in northern England.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Æthelfrith's victory at the Battle of Chester significantly weakened the influence of native Britons in northern England, paving the way for the unification of Northumbria under his rule. His military campaigns against the Britons and Gaels had lasting regional implications.
